content:
I feel motivated to work on resolving the defeq abuse between (restrictScalars f).obj M and M for a M : ModuleCat S. See PR #19511 by @Anne Baanen (second bullet point). There's also lots of TODO's mentioning this in ModuleCat/ChangeOfRings.lean and in a few other files.

The current state means we need a lot of explicit type hints when using ModuleCat.ofHom in combination with restrictScalars, as the module instance on (restrictScalars f).obj M is a non-standard one given by Module.compHom M f. See also the awkward statements of docs#ModuleCat.restrictScalars.smul_def and docs#ModuleCat.restrictScalars.smul_def'.

Instead, we probably want explicit ModuleCat morphisms going between M and (restrictScalars f).obj M. At first I thought I could use the already existing docs#RestrictScalars, which is a type synonym made precisely for this purpose (actually, should that be a one-field structure now?). However, RestrictScalars takes in an Algebra R S instance, which means it requires CommSemiring R. Meanwhile, for docs#ModuleCat.restrictScalars, we are working with [Ring R] [Ring S] {f : R →+* S}, so these aren't compatible.

What's the correct way forward here? Make a new type synonym (or one-field structure) similar to docs#RestrictScalars, but that works without the commutativity assumption? That would mean some duplication. Are there other options?
Do you mean "explicit (Semi)LinearMaps going between M and (restrictScalars f).obj M"?
One could do it at the level of docs#RestrictScalars, then it would be LinearMaps, but M and (restrictScalars f).obj M both live in ModuleCat.
But one of them in ModuleCat R and the other in ModuleCat S, so its not the same category.

Right, so it's semi linear maps then.

I've started to experiment with generalizing RestrictScalars in #38784. Probably RestrictScalars should be refactored to a one-field structure eventually, but that change is orthogonal to this generalization.

One of the difficulties is that in the proofs involving the restriction of scalars, we often need to transform a RingHom into an Algebra instance, and get Module/IsScalarTower instances. I do not know how to fix this (and similar issues for the extension of scalars), but any progress on this matter would be welcome!
Does algebraize not help here? Or maybe it can be extended to support that?
